guardian.title: ‘Give him any award, and he’ll come running’: Narendra Modi racks up honours on overseas trips
guardian.description:
Indian prime minister has a habit of collecting awards on his travels, some as their first and only recipient

As Narendra Modi touched down in Seychelles over the weekend, the archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean swiftly bestowed one of its “highest” honours upon the Indian prime minister.

Modi beamed as he accepted the Guardian of the Blue Horizon award from Patrick Herminie, the Seychelles president, complete with a trophy and certificate.

guardian.description:
Authorities say rainy season getting deadlier, with Ghana reporting 13 dead and floods hitting Benin, Togo and Nigeria

Floods in Côte d’Ivoire have killed 59 people since May, the communication minister told a cabinet meeting in Abidjan.

There are fears the toll could further rise as rescue teams continue to search for victims during the rainy season, which runs from May until July, the minister, Amadou Coulibaly, added.

guardian.description:
Report accuses paramilitary force of crimes including ethnic cleansing in systemic campaign against civilians

The Sudanese paramilitary Rapid Support Forces committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing during its campaign to capture El Fasher, Amnesty International has alleged.

guardian.description:
Fears of resurgence of HIV/Aids amid loss of access to PrEP drugs as at least 40 people arrested in ‘toxic’ climate

A “witch-hunt” is under way in Niger, where dozens of people have been arrested for homosexuality in the west African state following the introduction of a new penal code earlier this year.

Up to 40 people have been arrested and 16 men, including high-ranking military officials, have been imprisoned across the country, according to local media.

A 43-year-old security guard who survived last week’s devastating earthquakes in Venezuela thanks to a pocket of air in his workstation cabin has been pulled from the collapsed basement of a shopping centre amid huge cheers from international rescue teams.

Doctors in Canada say a child who awoke to find a bat resting on his nose and mouth while visiting an Ontario cottage later died of rabies, in an “exceedingly rare case” that highlights the need for better public awareness.

guardian.description:
Trump and US officials opted to keep USMCA alive on short leash of annual reviews rather than longer term renewal

Donald Trump has refused to renew the North American trade pact he once championed as his signature deal, opting instead to keep it alive on a short leash of annual reviews rather than committing to another 16 years.

guardian.description:

guardian.title: Canada to ​join Eurovision song contest from 2027
guardian.description:
Country is first to join since Australia in 2015 as event director says it ‘continues to welcome the world’

Canada will ​join the Eurovision song contest in 2027, becoming the first new ⁠participant since Australia in 2015, organisers have announced.

Participation is not limited to countries in geographic Europe and instead is open to all members of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), which Canada joined last week. Australia is an associate member.

guardian.title: China says man who flew plane into Beijing skyscraper had mental health problems
guardian.description:
Official statement offers the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual and fatal incident in Beijing

Chinese authorities said the man who flew a small plane into Beijing’s tallest skyscraper last week was a 66-year-old who had mental health problems.

The statement published on Thursday offered the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual incident that occurred in Beijing’s central business district on the evening of 26 June.

guardian.title: At least nine monks killed in Thailand after boy drives truck into procession
guardian.description:
Charges yet to be filed over incident in Mukdahan involving 11-year-old, as police seek to establish circumstances

An 11-year-old boy has driven his parents’ truck into a Buddhist procession in Thailand, killing at least nine monks.

CCTV footage shared by a local rescue group showed the moment the monks, wearing orange robes, were run over as they walked in procession along a road. The timestamp on the footage was shortly before 11am local time on Thursday.

guardian.title: Papua separatists kill American pilot in ‘message’ to US and Indonesia
guardian.description:
Rebels shoot pilot and set his civilian ⁠plane on fire amid long-running low-level battle for independence in region

rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has launched a clinical trial of experimental Ebola treatments as the outbreak continues to spread in the north-east of the country.

rfi.title: France reports sharp rise in deaths after record June heatwave
rfi.description: France recorded a rise of nearly 30 percent in deaths during the week beginning 22 June, the peak of the country's record-breaking heatwave, the public health authority said on Friday.

rfi.title: Belgium opens up Congo archives amid global minerals race
rfi.description: From century-old maps to meticulous field notes, Belgium is sitting on a trove of geological records on colonial-era Congo – a coveted archive it is working to open up amid a global scramble for critical minerals.

rfi.title: What can France learn from Spain's heatwave protection for workers?
rfi.description: As French workers face record-breaking temperatures, attention is turning to Spain, where measures introduced to deal with extreme weather are inspiring a proposal for climate leave in France.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Algeria 2-0 to move into World Cup last 16
rfi.description: Breel Embolo scored in the first half, Dan Ndoye tallied at the start of the second half and Switzerland advanced to the World Cup's round of 16 with a 2-0 victory over Algeria on Thursday night in Vancouver.

rfi.title: US shows ‘increasingly blatant’ bias over DRC peace deal, says Rwandan minister
rfi.description: The fragile peace process between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo is under renewed pressure, as the United States imposes fresh sanctions over alleged links to mineral trafficking from areas controlled by M23 rebels. Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe tells RFI Kigali is being unfairly blamed – arguing that the Congolese government has failed to meet its own commitments under the US-brokered peace deal.

rfi.title: Wildfires spread across southern France, as heatwave reignites forest concerns
rfi.description: Wildfires have broken out across southern France, forcing evacuations and stretching firefighting teams as the country prepares for the third heatwave of the summer, with the country's forests under increasing threat from climate change and disputes over logging.

rfi.title: World Bank drops climate funding target, raising fears for Africa
rfi.description: The World Bank has abandoned its target of directing 45 percent of its financing to projects that help tackle climate change, prompting warnings that poorer countries – especially in Africa – could receive less support to adapt to a warming world.

rfi.title: Paris death penalty congress warns abolition cannot be taken for granted
rfi.description: The fight to abolish the death penalty remains "eminently contemporary", French President Emmanuel Macron said as campaigners, judges and former death row prisoners gathered in Paris this week for the World Congress Against the Death Penalty, amid rising executions worldwide and renewed support for capital punishment in some democracies.

rfi.title: Podcast: Adapting to heat, France's fitness boom, Paris Mosque at 100
rfi.description: As France's record-breaking heatwave last week raises questions about how the country will have to adapt to a warming climate, we look at what that could mean for French culture. We also explore the country's growing interest in fitness – driven in part by its most popular YouTuber – and examine how the Grand Mosque of Paris, which marks its centenary this year, became both a symbol of Islam in France and a recurring source of political tension.

rfi.title: Senegal midfielder Gueye refuses to play while coaching staff stay in charge
rfi.description: Senegal midfielder Pape Gueye announced he will not play any more international games for his country while the squad's coaching staff remains in charge.

rfi.title: Google loses final appeal against EU’s record €4.1bn anti-trust fine
rfi.description: The European Union’s top court has dismissed Google’s final appeal against a record €4.1 billion anti-trust fine, confirming one of Brussels’ most significant victories in its long-running effort to rein in Big Tech.

rfi.title: Ramos strikes late to take Portugal past Croatia into last-16 at World Cup
rfi.description: Gonçalo Ramos scored a stoppage time winner to send Portugal past Croatia into a last 16 showdown with Spain.

rfi.title: Algeria votes in parliamentary elections amid public apathy and football fever
rfi.description: Algerians are voting in parliamentary elections on Thursday, with cost of living concerns, questions over political freedoms and the national football team’s World Cup run all competing for public attention.

rfi.title: France confirms dates for 2027 presidential election
rfi.description: France will hold the first round of its next presidential election on 18 April 2027 and the runoff on 2 May after the government formally approved the dates at Wednesday's cabinet meeting.

rfi.title: France advances assisted dying law with strict rules and safeguards
rfi.description: France's National Assembly has approved a new version of a bill creating a legal right to assisted dying, bringing the country closer to a major change in end-of-life care. The legislation sets out who could qualify, how requests would be made and the safeguards designed to prevent abuse of the law.

rfi.title: Sudan's RSF paramilitaries accused of crimes against humanity in El Fasher
rfi.description: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing while deliberately targeting children during their campaign to seize El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur state, Amnesty International said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Mali's war on civilians deepens as alliances shift, HRW says
rfi.description: Human Rights Watch (HRW) says the army, allied militias and Islamist armed groups have all committed abuses with impunity since the attacks in northern Mali in April.

lemonde.title: Canicule de juin 2026 : les décès ont augmenté de presque 30 %, selon Santé publique France
lemonde.description: La tendance est particulièrement frappante en Ile-de-France, avec une hausse de plus de 62 % des décès sur la semaine dernière. Une progression semblable a été signalée dans les Pays de la Loire.

lemonde.title: Situation de crise pour l’agriculture française, entre deux canicules : « Tout le monde a la boule au ventre »
lemonde.description: Cultures brûlées, élevages décimés, baisse de production à deux chiffres pour certaines filières : les exploitants dressent le bilan des très fortes chaleurs de la fin juin et redoutent déjà les suivantes.

lemonde.title: Vladimir Poutine, la tentation de la fuite en avant
lemonde.description: Malgré une économie exsangue et la lassitude de la population, le président russe maintient ses exigences maximalistes à l’égard de l’Ukraine, refusant toute option diplomatique pour mettre fin à la guerre.

lemonde.title: « Sans investisseurs, les nouveaux venus finissent par couler » : face à Instagram ou TikTok, la difficile survie des plateformes européennes
lemonde.description: Comment concurrencer les réseaux américains ou chinois ? De nombreuses aventures ont jusqu’ici mené à des échecs ou à des succès mineurs. Mais alors que l’on parle plus que jamais de souveraineté numérique, des initiatives continuent à voir le jour, en quête d’appui des pouvoirs publics.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies dans le sud de la France : six départements placés en « danger très élevé » par Météo-France
lemonde.description: Plusieurs départs de feu ont eu lieu depuis mercredi dans les Pyrénées-Orientales, l’Aude, l’Hérault, le Gard, le Vaucluse et les Bouches-du-Rhône. Le plus important brûle toujours dans la zone de Pouzols-Minervois.

lemonde.title: « L’incroyable “remontada” des films sur de Gaulle, passés en quelques jours de bides à succès, renvoie au paradoxe que porte le héros de la France libre »
lemonde.description: Le premier volet de « La Bataille de Gaulle », sorti le 3 juin, a connu des débuts décevants, avant de voir ses entrées remonter en flèche, entraînant le second volet dans son sillage. Un phénomène exceptionnel, porté par la canicule et le bouche-à-oreille, et important tant le film résonne avec l’actualité, estime Michel Guerrin, rédacteur en chef au « Monde », dans sa chronique.

lemonde.title: L’Espagne est « bel et bien là » : la presse internationale salue la maestria retrouvée de la Roja à la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: Enfin emballante après des débuts poussifs, la Roja a impressionné, jeudi, lors de sa victoire contre l’Autriche. En huitièmes de finale, les Espagnols devront se méfier du Portugal de Cristiano Ronaldo, qui a marqué et initié le retour des siens contre la Croatie.

lemonde.title: Funérailles d’Ali Khamenei : des millions d’Iraniens attendus à Téhéran pour l’hommage au Guide suprême, qui commencera samedi
lemonde.description: La dépouille d’Ali Khamenei est arrivée vendredi sur le lieu de ses funérailles à Téhéran. Les autorités attendent entre 15 millions et 20 millions de participants rien que dans la capitale, devenue une ville-forteresse.

lemonde.title: Trois recettes fraîches pour l’été, (presque) sans cuisson
lemonde.description: Gaspacho de concombre, thon mariné et pêche pochée sont au menu concocté par Julien Dumas, chef du restaurant parisien Zostera, pour un été léger.

lemonde.title: En Syrie, le président Ahmed Al-Charaa rattrapé par la menace terroriste
lemonde.description: Une explosion a tué neuf personnes et fait vingt blessés, jeudi, dans un café du centre de Damas. Non revendiquée, cette attaque est la plus sanglante qu’ait connue la capitale syrienne depuis l’attentat suicide contre une église grecque orthodoxe, en juin 2025, qui avait fait 25 morts.

lemonde.title: « Le Monde » répond à vos questions sur sa ligne éditoriale, sa gouvernance et la vie de sa rédaction
lemonde.description: « Rendez-vous avec Le Monde » : comme chaque mois, Gilles van Kote, directeur délégué aux relations avec les lecteurs, répond en direct aux questions des internautes concernant la couverture de l’actualité et la vie du journal.

lemonde.title: L’identité, un thème à haut risque pour la gauche
lemonde.description: Avec le concept de « nouvelle France », Jean-Luc Mélenchon a placé la question identitaire au cœur de la campagne présidentielle de la gauche. Avec le risque de légitimer le discours de l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: Adoptions forcées au Royaume-Uni : Keir Starmer présente des excuses officielles
lemonde.description: Plus de 185 000 enfants nés de mères non mariées ont été adoptés en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles entre 1949 et 1976. Une « tache indélébile dans notre histoire », a déclaré le premier ministre travailliste, jeudi, à quelques jours de son départ de Downing Street.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, inquiétude sur le sort de centaines de milliers d’Haïtiens susceptibles d’être renvoyés dans leur pays
lemonde.description: Plus de 330 000 immigrés haïtiens risquent de perdre leur permis de séjour et d’être « renvoyés vers la violence » qui fait rage dans leur pays d’origine, après la révocation par l’administration Trump de leur statut de protection temporaire, s’inquiète l’ONG Human Rights Watch.

lemonde.description: Des chercheurs ont élaboré un système permettant d’expliquer l’étirement des tissus cellulaires, un mécanisme basé sur l’intercalation de cellules.

lemonde.description: Le marché sur le littoral hexagonal reste dynamique, mais les acheteurs sont exigeants et prennent davantage en compte les critères environnementaux.

Face à cette nouvelle escalade, Volodymyr Zelensky renouvelle son appel à l'aide des États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : à Kiev, poursuite des opérations de secours après les plus grosses frappes russes
france24fr.description: Les secouristes poursuivent leurs recherches à Kiev après les frappes russes les plus meurtrières contre la capitale depuis le début de la guerre, qui ont fait au moins 30 morts, près de 100 blessés et laissé dix personnes portées disparues. La ville reste enveloppée par la fumée des incendies, tandis que les perspectives de règlement diplomatique demeurent au point mort, l'Ukraine a d'ailleurs promis une riposte. Les précisions d'Emmanuelle Chaze à Kiev.

france24fr.title: Culte de la personnalité autour de Trump lors des célébrations du 250e anniversaire des États-Unis
france24fr.description: Pièce de monnaie, passeport... et bientôt le mont Rushmore ? À l'occasion des célébrations en grande pompe du 250e anniversaire de l'indépendance des États-Unis, le président Donald Trump est omniprésent. Une mise en scène qui pousse certains observateurs à dénoncer un véritable culte de la personnalité. Mais malgré les festivités, une partie des Américains boude les célébrations, un revers pour le président. L'analyse d'Antoine Mariotti pour France 24.

france24fr.title: "Une Russie forte, ou il n'y aura plus de Russie" : l'appel à la nation de Vladimir Poutine
france24fr.description: Alors que la Russie subit des rationnements de carburant à cause des frappes ukrainiennes contre les infrastructures pétrolières russes, Vladimir Poutine reconnaît un "déficit non critique". Le président l'affirme : l'Ukraine aurait lancé une "campagne informationnelle" destinée à "fracturer" la société russe. Face au parti Russie Unie entré en campagne pour les élections législatives de septembre, il a appelé dimanche dernier à une "Russie forte", faute de quoi il n'y aurait "plus de Russie". S

france24fr.title: Canicule : incendie dans le sud de la France, les habitants évacués
france24fr.description: Le plus gros incendie enregistré cette saison brûle depuis mercredi après-midi dans l’Aude et l’Hérault. Attisé par le vent, il a déjà parcouru environ 900 hectares. Dans un contexte de vigilance rouge canicule, les habitants sont appelés à évacuer.

france24fr.title: L'actu en dessin : les frappes ukrainiennes mettent la Russie à sec
france24fr.description: En représailles aux frappes russes, l'Ukraine a multiplié les attaques sur le territoire russe, ciblant notamment les raffineries et les dépôts de pétrole. Pénuries de carburant, files d'attente aux stations-service et critiques grandissantes : la guerre voulue par Vladimir Poutine pèse désormais sur l'arrière russe, malgré des représailles toujours plus meurtrières contre l'Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : un Argentine - Cap-Vert à Miami, dans le jardin de Lionel Messi
france24fr.description: L'Argentine championne du monde affronte, vendredi, le Cap-Vert, le Petit Poucet de la compétition, à Miami. C'est dans cette ville que Lionel Messi s'est installé après son départ du PSG en 2023. Avec l'Inter Miami, il vole de succès en succès et dit se sentir bien dans le sud de la Floride, où l’espagnol est la première langue pour 75 % de la population.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : le Portugal élimine la Croatie au bout du suspense
france24fr.description: Ces 16es de finale de Coupe du monde sont pleins de rebondissements. Mené 1-0, le Portugal a renversé la Croatie grâce à un but de Gonçalo Ramos dans le temps additionnel. Cristiano Ronaldo avait auparavant égalisé sur penalty. Les Portugais retrouveront l’Espagne en huitièmes de finale.

france24fr.title: En France, une augmentation des décès de presque 30 % la semaine de la canicule
france24fr.description: La canicule qui a frappé la France la dernière semaine de juin a provoqué au moins 2 025 décès de plus que la semaine précédente, soit une hausse de près de 30 % à l'échelle nationale, a annoncé vendredi ​la ministre ‌de la Santé, Stéphanie Rist, ⁠en citant un bilan encore partiel de Santé publique France. À Paris, le taux de surmortalité est d'au moins 62 %.

france24fr.title: 250 ans d'indépendance des États-Unis : pourquoi la France a misé sur la révolution américaine
france24fr.description: Le soutien français à la révolution américaine ne naît pas le 4 juillet 1776. Bien avant la Déclaration d'indépendance, la monarchie de Louis XVI voit dans la rébellion des Treize Colonies une occasion d'affaiblir son ennemi britannique. Entre revanche géopolitique et idéaux des Lumières, retour sur les origines d'une alliance décisive.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: L'Algérie éliminée par la Suisse, le Portugal qui renverse la Croatie et L'Espagne qui surclasse l'Autriche. Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Liesse populaire et hargne sur le terrain : qui est le Paraguay, futur adversaire des Bleus ?
france24fr.description: Le Paraguay a créé la sensation en éliminant l'Allemagne en 16es de finale. Un authentique exploit, qui a été célébré par un jour férié dans le pays sud-américain alors que son sélectionneur a qualifié ses joueurs de "légendes". Un succès bâti sur la "garra guarani", un état d'esprit hargneux en toutes circonstances. L'équipe de France est prévenue.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Algérie éliminée par la Suisse en 16es de finale
Mondial 2026 : une Algérie en mal d'inspiration éliminée par la Suisse en 16es de finale
france24fr.description: L'Algérie a été éliminée par une équipe de Suisse chirurgicale (2-0) vendredi à Vancouver en 16es de finale du Mondial. En cinq participations à une Coupe du monde, les Fennecs n’ont jamais remporté un match à élimination directe.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la météo, l’autre adversaire des Bleus ?
france24fr.description: Alerte canicule pour le prochain rendez-vous des Bleus en 8e de finale face au Paraguay. Cependant, malgré les fortes chaleurs prévues samedi 4 juillet à Philadelphie, Bradley Barcola et Jules Koundé assurent que l'équipe est préparée pour jouer dans ces conditions.

france24fr.title: Suisse - Algérie en direct : la Nati prend le large face aux Fennecs
france24fr.description: Solide à défaut d'être vraiment séduisante, la Suisse se mesure à l'Algérie d'Ibrahim Maza, vendredi, au BC Place de Vancouver au Canada en 16es de finale de la Coupe du monde 2026. Suivez ce match en live grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: En direct : des dignitaires religieux rendent hommage au défunt guide suprême Khamenei
france24fr.description: Le corps du guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei, tué dans des frappes américano-israéliennes le 28 février, est arrivé dans la vaste enceinte religieuse de la capitale iranienne où se dérouleront ses funérailles. Les autorités attendent entre 15 et 20 millions de participants rien qu'à Téhéran pour cet hommage de trois jours, qui débute samedi. Les négociations entre Téhéran et Washington reprendront ensuite. Suivez notre direct.

zeit.title: Erneuter Stopp: Schleifähre «Missunde III» pausiert wegen Niedrigwasser
Russland und Wladimir Putin: »Russlands Krieg gegen die Ukraine richtet sich gegen Russland selbst«
zeit.description: Drohnen in Moskau, rasant steigende Lebenshaltungskosten, Benzinengpässe: Der Druck auf Wladimir Putin steigt. Ist das der Anfang vom Ende des russischen Präsidenten?

zeit.title: Erneuerbare Energie: Landkreis genehmigt Bau von Pumpspeicherwerk Riedl
Staatsschutz ermittelt: Gewalt in Cottbus: Scheibe von Grünen-Büro zerstört
Wirtschaft in den USA: Das getarnte Freiheitsversprechen der Tech-Milliardäre
zeit.description: Der Paläolibertarismus der amerikanischen Tech-Elite macht sich auch in Europa breit. Er schwächt den Staat und nur ein scheinbares Ideal: Freiheit für alle.

zeit.title: War es Mord?: Nach Fund einer Leiche – Mordanklage gegen Verdächtigen
Trauer: Seeler-Witwe Ilka mit 89 Jahren gestorben
Obdachlosigkeit: Wenig Wohnungslose in Sachsen-Anhalt untergebracht
NSU-Prozess in Dresden: Anklage fordert 4 Jahre Haft für Freundin von Beate Zschäpe
Alexandru Munteanu: Ministerpräsident von Moldau tritt zurück
zeit.description: Er könne sein Amt nicht mehr in Einklang mit seinen Prinzipien ausüben, sagt Moldaus Ministerpräsident Alexandru Munteanu. Mit ihm muss die gesamte Regierung abtreten.

zeit.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Das sind die Spitzenkandidierenden in Sachsen-Anhalt
zeit.description: In Sachsen-Anhalt könnte die AfD die absolute Mehrheit holen. Die Union hofft dennoch auf das Ministerpräsidentenamt. Die SPD bangt um den Einzug. Die Kandidierenden

zeit.title: Wissenschaftler gegen AfD: »Das ist ein Akt der Notwehr«
zeit.description: Wissenschaft im Widerstandsmodus: Forschende rufen zum Widerstand gegen die AfD auf. Ein Gespräch über den Protest und Faschisierungstendenzen in der Gesellschaft.

zeit.title: Krankschreibung: Jens Spahn verteidigt schärfere Regeln für Krankschreibungen
zeit.description: »Man sitzt auf der Bettkante und überlegt: Passt das heute?« Spahn fordert bei Krankschreibungen Fairness unter Kollegen. Klingbeil verspricht »vernünftige Regelung«.

zeit.title: Reformen der Bundesregierung: Das reicht noch nicht!
zeit.description: Die Bundesregierung stößt richtige Reformen an. Die Erleichterung darüber sollte aber nicht in Begeisterung umschlagen. Das würde uns Wohlstand kosten.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Protestcamp gegen Datencenter in Benken wird geräumt
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

nzz.title: Frisiert, nicht frittiert: wie Chinas Vierbeiner zu «pelzigen Kindern» wurden
nzz.description: Ein entführter – und später verspeister – Border Collie löst in China eine Welle der Empörung aus. Der Fall zeigt vor allem eins: wie aus einer Nation von vermeintlichen Hundeverzehrern längst ein Volk von Hundeverehrern geworden ist.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Renk übernimmt britischen U-Boot-Zulieferer +++ Tesla liefert deutlich mehr Autos aus als erwartet
LIVE-TICKER - Tote und Verletzte bei neuen russischen Angriffen auf die Ukraine +++ Kiew ruft für Freitag Trauertag aus
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Emotionen und besondere Momente – Einblicke in die WM in Bildern
nzz.description: Drei Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.title: Nach dem «Fall Heiniger»: Eine «Anstandsregel» soll die Berufswahl für ehemalige Zürcher Regierungsräte einschränken
nzz.description: Die neuen Vorschriften sollen das Vertrauen in politische Institutionen stärken. Doch die FDP sieht die Wirtschaftsfreiheit gefährdet.

nzz.title: Tierschutzfall Ramiswil (SO): Nicht alle Hunde hätten getötet werden müssen
nzz.description: Auf einem Hof schläferte der Veterinärdienst im November 122 Hunde ein. Die Halterin hatte ihre Tiere schwer vernachlässigt. Jetzt kommt eine externe Untersuchung zu dem Schluss, dass den Behörden das Risikobewusstsein fehlte.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Nagelsmann-Rücktritt: DFB-Aufsichtsrat tagt +++ Public Viewing um 5 Uhr früh
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Erdbeben in Venezuela: Millionen-Fonds für den Wiederaufbau geplant +++ Inzwischen fast 2300 Opfer gezählt
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten richteten zwei Erdbeben in Venezuela verheerende Schäden an. Rettungskräfte suchen unter den Trümmern nach Überlebenden. Über das Ausmass der Schäden ist wenig bekannt.

nzz.title: Kafikränzli, Morgestraich und Fondue-Party: Die Schweiz feiert ein Fussballfest in den Morgenstunden
nzz.description: Im ganzen Land strömen die Fans für das Spiel der Schweiz gegen Algerien um 5 Uhr früh in Public Viewings, Bars und Hinterhöfe. Die NZZ war in Zürich, Basel, Bern, Olten und Baden live dabei.

nzz.title: Lucid Air Sapphire: Die amerikanische E-Limousine bietet Rennsport und Reisekomfort in einem
nzz.description: Mit 1250 PS, 700 Kilometern Reichweite und 900 Litern Stauraum macht der Lucid Air Sapphire der europäischen Elite von Porsche und Mercedes Konkurrenz. Der amerikanische Stromer ist schneller, geräumiger und günstiger als der Taycan Turbo GT.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Staatsbegräbnis für Ali Khamenei +++ Medienberichte über Beginn von indirekten US-Iran-Gesprächen in Katar
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar vereinbarten die beiden Länder Mitte Juni eine Waffenruhe. Doch diese ist fragil. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Murat Yakins Equipe schlägt ihren ehemaligen Coach und Algerien souverän mit 2:0 – der Ticker zum Nachlesen
nzz.description: In Vancouver gelang der Mannschaft um Granit Xhaka endlich ein Sieg in einem WM-K.-o.-Spiel. Gefährdet war er zu keinem Zeitpunkt der Partie: Das Schweizer Nationalteam trat effizient, abgeklärt und reif auf.

nzz.title: Mit fast unheimlicher Souveränität: Erstmals seit 1938 gewinnt die Schweiz an einer WM eine Partie in der K.-o.-Phase
nzz.description: Der Sieg im WM-Sechzehntelfinal gerät nie ernsthaft in Gefahr. Beim 2:0 gegen Algerien sorgt abermals der Spektakelspieler Johan Manzambi für den Unterschied.

nzz.title: Der Seppenverein Erlinsbach löst sich nach 150 Jahren auf. Grund: Seppenmangel
nzz.description: In der zweiten Hälfte des 19. Jahrhunderts wurden in der Schweiz zahllose Vornamenvereine gegründet; nun verschwinden sie. Es ist auch das Ende eines beispiellosen sozialen Experiments.

spiegel.title: 250-Jahr-Feier der USA: Von Trumps Pracht-Bühne fallen während der Probe Stücke ab
spiegel.description: Es ist die neueste Panne bei der pannenreichen Feier zum 250. Geburtstag der USA: Um ein Haar wären probende Tänzer auf der Hauptbühne von herabfallenden Teilen getroffen worden.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Deutscher Wetterdienst korrigiert Temperaturrekord nach oben
spiegel.description: Möckern-Drewitz in Sachsen-Anhalt bekommt nachträglich den Titel als heißester Ort Deutschlands. In einer Umfrage fordert nun eine Mehrheit Konsequenzen aus der jüngsten Hitzewelle.

spiegel.title: Manfred Vorderwülbecke: Der »Blickpunkt Sport«-Erfinder ist tot
spiegel.description: Manfred Vorderwülbecke hat mit seinen Ideen den TV-Sport geprägt. In den Siebzigerjahren holte er etwa Ski-alpin-Olympiasiegerin Rosi Mittermaier als Expertin vor die Kamera und bewies damit Weitsicht. Nun ist er gestorben.

spiegel.title: Polymarket: Diese Wettplattform lockt Jugendliche an und zieht ihnen das Geld aus der Tasche
spiegel.description: 50 Milliarden Dollar könnten mit Wetten zur Fußball-WM umgesetzt werden, so viel wie noch nie. Dick im Geschäft: die umstrittene Plattform Polymarket, Schutzmechanismen für Jugendliche werden geschickt umgangen.

spiegel.title: Anti-AfD-Proteste: Wer Parteitage blockiert, schädigt die Demokratie - Meinung
spiegel.description: Ein breites Bündnis will verhindern, dass die rechtsextreme AfD ihren Parteitag in Erfurt abhalten kann. Das ist falsch.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Zahl der Adoptionen sinkt auf niedrigsten Stand seit Wiedervereinigung
spiegel.description: In Deutschland werden immer weniger Kinder adoptiert: Im vergangenen Jahr waren es bundesweit etwa 3500. Einen gegenläufigen Trend registrierten die Statistiker besonders in einer Familienform.

spiegel.title: Gökay Akbulut: Linkenabgeordnete erhält Strafbefehl nach Zugstreit
spiegel.description: Die Bundestagsabgeordnete Gökay Akbulut hat im Januar 2025 berichtet, sie sei in einem Zug angegriffen worden. Danach gab es Zweifel an der Darstellung, und es wurde auch gegen die Politikerin ermittelt – nun gibt es eine Entscheidung.

spiegel.title: USA feiern Unabhängigkeitserklärung: »Dieser 250. Geburtstag ist eine verpasste Chance«
spiegel.description: Washington ist geschmückt, doch die Stimmung in den USA bleibt gedämpft. Der Historiker Jason Steinhauer erklärt, warum die Jubiläumsfeier hinter den Erwartungen bleibt und wie Trump sie politisch auflädt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Kid Rock erzählt von nächtlichen Anrufen beim Präsidenten
spiegel.description: Der wahre Irrsinn ist ja, dass man ihm die Geschichte sofort abnimmt: Trump-Freund Kid Rock hat verraten, wie er angeblich am liebsten mit dem US-Präsidenten kommuniziert. Nämlich nachts am Telefon. Mit ein paar Bier im Kopf.

spiegel.title: Verbraucherschützer warnen vor falschen BKA-Mails
spiegel.description: Mit Drohungen und gefälschten Briefköpfen versuchen angebliche BKA-Mitarbeiter, Bürger zur Herausgabe sensibler Ausweisdaten zu bringen. Verbraucherschützer warnen vor dieser Betrugsmasche.

spiegel.title: New York: Mutmaßlicher Tibet-Aktivist stirbt nach Selbstverbrennung vor dem Uno-Hauptquartier
spiegel.description: Videos zeigen, wie sich ein Mann neben einer Tibet-Flagge vor der Zentrale der Vereinten Nationen in Brand setzt. Er starb an seinen schweren Verletzungen. Offenbar handelte es sich um eine Protestaktion gegen China.

spiegel.title: Mönchengladbach: Lkw-Auflieger mit Gülle umgekippt – Straße gesperrt
spiegel.description: In der Nacht ist ein Lkw in Mönchengladbach von der Straße abgekommen. Der mit Gülle beladene Auflieger stürzte um, die Ladung lief aus. Das machte eine aufwendige Reinigung notwendig.

spiegel.title: Nürnberg: Nach Hitzeschäden – erste Straßenbahnstrecke wieder freigegeben
spiegel.description: Wegen verklumpter Fugenmasse in den Schienen stellte Nürnberg den Straßenbahnbetrieb am vergangenen Wochenende ein. Nun läuft er zumindest auf einer Strecke wieder an.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Vier Tote und zehn Verletzte nach russischen Drohnen- und Raketenangriffen
spiegel.description: Russland hat erneut mit Drohnen und Raketen die Ukraine beschossen. In einer Industriestadt gibt es schwere Schäden an der Infrastruktur, in einer Kleinstadt stirbt ein knapp zweijähriges Mädchen.

spiegel.title: US-Regierung muss entfernte Sklaverei-Denkmäler nicht wieder aufstellen – vorerst
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hatte sein Innenministerium angewiesen, sämtliche Gedenkstätten, -tafeln, Statuen und Ähnliches darauf zu überprüfen, ob sie die Geschichte der USA in ein schlechtes Licht rücken.

spiegel.title: US-Techkonzerne dominieren die Börsen – Deutsche verlieren den Anschluss
spiegel.description: Der KI-Boom hat auch gravierende Auswirkungen auf die Börse. Die US-Techkonzerne bauen ihren Vorsprung in der Rangliste der wertvollsten Konzerne der Welt weiter aus. Aus deutscher Sicht kann da nur Siemens mithalten.

spiegel.title: Koalition will Reformpaket nicht zerreden lassen
spiegel.description: Am Reformpaket gibt es von vielen Seiten Kritik, aus der Wirtschaft, von Gewerkschaften, von Verbänden. Die Regierungskoalition will die Pläne aber weitgehend umsetzen, auch wenn es noch einige offene Fragen gibt.

spiegel.title: Iran: Donald Trump hatte offenbar Sorge, dass Israel Teherans Topdiplomaten während Verhandlungsrunde gezielt töten lässt
spiegel.description: Pakistan hat im April die iranische Delegation nach indirekten Verhandlungen mit den USA durch den eigenen Luftraum eskortiert – mit zwei Dutzend Kampfjets. Der Grund: Angst um das Leben von Abbas Araghchi und Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

observador.title: "A Europa é os EUA com atraso"
observador.description: O Major-general Arnaut Moreira sublinha que o sonho americano é uma atração pela liberdade e sucesso. Ainda acrescenta que a Europa replica os modelos dos EUA com alguns anos de atraso.

observador.title: 10h. Exames. Ministério da Educação adia segunda fase
observador.description: Os professores têm até dia 14 para corrigir as provas. As pautas são afixadas no dia 17. A 2ª fase dos exames arranca no dia 20 de julho. Ainda neste jornal, atualizamos informação sobre os incêndios.

observador.title: Colisão em Guimarães causa uma morte e dois feridos
observador.description: Uma mulher perdeu a vida e um homem ficou em estado grave na sequência de um acidente em Conde, Guimarães, na noite de quinta-feira.

observador.title: Incêndios. "Erros do ano passado vão ser cometidos este ano"
observador.description: António Nunes, presidente da Liga dos Bombeiros, afirma que medidas tomadas para combater incêndios não são suficientes. Diz que quando é necessário tomar medidas é "a correr atrás do prejuízo".

observador.title: EUA celebram 250 anos sem programa especial em Portugal
observador.description: Apesar do número redondo, que simboliza a independência americana da Grã-Bretanha, a Embaixada dos EUA confirmou à Lusa que "não estão previstas iniciativas específicas para esta data".

observador.title: Mundial: De "guerreiros feios" a whiskys com gelo
observador.description: No mundo do futebol, o talento nem sempre vem com beleza - que o digam os "feios" de Nuremberga. Entre o Messi parecer pequeno e treinadores a pedir whisky, há histórias que dão baile a qualquer jogo.

observador.title: Montenegro no Mundial: faz sentido, com o país em alerta?
observador.description: Carneiro "queimou-se" com as casas vazias e o IVA dos filetes é um labirinto total. Com o país em alerta e o governo a prever dias terríveis, Montenegro tinha mesmo de ir ver a bola a Toronto?

observador.title: Dia 23 do Mundial-2026. Portugal passa aos oitavos de final
observador.description: Portugal vence à Croácia por 2-1 e vai defrontar Espanha nos oitavos de final. Selecionador alemão apresenta a demissão após derrota com o Paraguai. Ronaldo garante que ainda não decidiu reforma.

observador.title: 9h. Vaga de Calor. PM diz que próximos dias serão difíceis
observador.description: O governo proíbe o acesso a certos espaços e caminhos florestais, bem como a realização de queimadas e de trabalho com maquinaria. Ainda, damos destaque à vitória de Portugal frente à Croácia por 2-1

observador.title: Notas dos exames nacionais adiadas para 17 de julho
observador.description: Ministério anuncia novo calendário após problemas na correção dos exames. Afixação das notas e segunda fase adiadas mas calendário de acesso ao ensino superior mantém-se.

observador.title: Murakami nas livrarias do Japão com "A história de Kaho"
observador.description: "Kaho, autora de livros ilustrados, é uma jovem comum. Mas começam a acontecer coisas estranhas", disse Murakami sobre o livro. O romance do escritor chegou esta sexta-feira às livrarias do Japão.

observador.title: Livreiro detido na China morre em Taipé
observador.description: Lam Wing-kee morreu na sequência de uma recidiva de um cancro. Era dono da Causeway Bay Books, especializada em obras críticas a líderes chineses.

observador.title: Alguma revolução sobrevive 250 anos? Apenas uma: a americana
observador.description: “Consideramos estas verdades evidentes por si mesmas, que todos os homens são criados iguais." Esta frase tem 250 anos, abre a Declaração de Independência dos Estados Unidos e ainda hoje a celebramos.

observador.title: David Catalán em Ílhavo e Marques'Almeida em Matosinhos
observador.description: O designer espanhol abriu os trabalhos na quinta-feira com uma coleção inspirada em coletes salva-vidas vintage. À noite, os Marques'Almeida fizeram uma rave de luxo em Matosinhos.

observador.title: Os heróis da seleção e a polémica das casas vazias
observador.description: Num jogo louco, Portugal passou aos oitavos e vai encontrar Espanha. Processos desmentem versão de Carneiro nas casas vazias. Banco de Portugal aperta regras no crédito. E, afinal, quem raptou o Zé?

observador.title: Imigrantes saem do sistema, mas saldo continua positivo

phys-org.title: Modest meat and dairy cuts could help Scotland lower emissions and keep diets affordable
phys-org.description: Modest changes to meat and dairy consumption could help Scotland meet climate goals while improving health and nutrition, research shows. A modeling study appearing in Nature Food found that using vegetables, beans and eggs instead of processed and unprocessed meat and dairy could deliver environmental and health benefits without increasing the overall cost of diets.

phys-org.title: Wildfires rage in southern France, 3,000 people evacuated
phys-org.description: Nearly 3,000 people have been evacuated in southwestern France as Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu sounded the alarm over an early outbreak of wildfires in the wake of a record-breaking heat wave.

phys-org.title: Japan deploys bear cameras in mountains as attacks surge
phys-org.description: Japan has begun installing hundreds of cameras in its northern mountains as part of a nationwide survey of the bear population following a surge in maulings, an official told AFP on Thursday.

phys-org.title: Two centuries on, experts unlock secrets of Red Sea and Gulf of Aden sailing chart
phys-org.description: Experts have unlocked secrets hidden for two hundred years in a beautiful navigational chart made for 18th century seafarers negotiating the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The paper scroll is evidence seafaring communities in the region used their own effective system of navigation that enabled trade and exchange between India, Arabia and the Horn of Africa in the age of sail, before the uptake of a more abstract, instrument-based navigation.

phys-org.title: Heat dome roasts eastern US ahead of holiday weekend
phys-org.description: Pools were packed and power grids strained as millions of Americans sweltered in stifling heat and humidity Thursday, with dangerous temperatures expected to hit major cities through the Fourth of July holiday weekend.

phys-org.title: Bottlenose dolphins in the Adriatic Sea seem to be heavily reliant on trawlers for food
phys-org.description: Bottlenose dolphins in the Adriatic Sea are spending much of their time following trawlers to scavenge for food, scientists say. The Adriatic seabed has been plowed by bottom trawlers for decades, resulting in ecosystem damage. Many apex predators are no longer present there. phys-org.title: Many students listen to music to focus and stay motivated while they study—but it doesn't always help
phys-org.description: Walk into any college library and you will likely see students wearing headphones and listening to music.

phys-org.title: Feline fleas carry bacteria linked to human disease in South Texas, study finds
phys-org.description: As human cases of flea-borne murine typhus continue to occur in South Texas, researchers are working to better understand the role cats and their fleas may play in the disease's transmission cycle.

phys-org.title: The center has shifted: Multifunctional facility in Japan reshapes where people linger
phys-org.description: Suburban city centers across Japan are gradually declining as residents shift to car-oriented shopping malls in outlying areas. Urban planners have sought to reverse this trend through urban catalytic projects, strategically placed facilities designed to trigger broader regeneration. Yet empirical evidence on whether such projects actually redirect people's stay behavior beyond the facility itself has remained scarce.

phys-org.title: Hantaviruses may have co-evolved with rodents for ages, helping explain silent spread
phys-org.description: What does a hantavirus do inside its rodent hosts? How do these viruses move through animal populations? And how is it that they cause almost no apparent symptoms in rodents, yet can be nearly fatal in humans? Specially Appointed Professor Hiroaki Kariwa has been studying hantaviruses at Hokkaido University for more than 35 years, and these are some of the questions that have driven his research. Over the years, his team has uncovered important insights into the ecology and evolution of hantavir

phys-org.title: Airborne AI spots underwater munitions in shallow seas with high precision
phys-org.description: A new airborne imaging approach can reliably detect unexploded weapons that lie in shallow coastal waters and remain an ongoing hazard to public safety, marine ecosystems and infrastructure worldwide. By combining advanced multispectral sensing with artificial intelligence, the researchers were able to identify underwater munitions with high confidence, even when they are partially hidden by sediment, biological growth or debris.

phys-org.title: Postwar research compact fueled U.S. prosperity for eight decades, argues commentary
phys-org.description: As the United States celebrates 250 years of independence, Science has published a commentary by Johns Hopkins University President Ron Daniels highlighting the impact of the reimagining of the American university pioneered by Johns Hopkins in the late 19th century—and how the benefits of that shift and the later emergence of the compact between research universities and the federal government have been integral to the nation's success and prosperity.

phys-org.title: This satellite constellation transformed earth science by creatively tuning in to GPS signals
phys-org.description: When NASA's Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System, or CYGNSS, launched into orbit in 2016, none of the University of Michigan Engineering researchers who developed the system expected it to transform earth science. They certainly had high hopes for the system's original mission to improve hurricane forecasting, but its ability to pick up reflected GPS signals also proved useful for much more.

phys-org.title: Nanozymes map nanoparticle routes inside live cells without genetic engineering
phys-org.description: Nanoparticles are widely used in medicine to deliver drugs, genes or imaging agents to specific parts of the body. Once a nanoparticle reaches a cell, however, many things can happen—it can reach its target, be degraded, interact with proteins that help transport it, or interact with proteins that hinder its transport.

phys-org.title: Simulation reveals how glaciers transported rocks across the Alps 24,000 years ago
phys-org.description: Many of the boulders scattered across the Swiss landscape did not originate where they now stand. Instead, they were carried by ice nearly 24,000 years ago. For the first time, researchers at the University of Lausanne (UNIL) have reconstructed the journeys of these giant rocks across the entire Alpine region using a simulation. The model makes it possible to visualize the paths taken by millions of rocks that helped shape today's landscapes.

phys-org.title: Beyond the 24-hour day: How employee biological clocks and beliefs drive workplace cooperation
phys-org.description: Employees' biological clocks do more than determine when they reach for coffee; they fundamentally shape how, when and why people help each other at work. A study published in Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes introduces the concept of "time-extension self-efficacy" (TESE)—an individual's belief in their ability to successfully wake up earlier or stay up later than usual.

phys-org.title: Coral loss may erase up to $3 billion in Hawaiʻi reef recreation by 2100
phys-org.description: Coral reef decline driven by climate change could cost Hawaiʻi residents between $1.8 billion and $3 billion in lost reef-related activities by 2100, according to a new study published in Ecological Economics. The research projects that these burdens will not fall equally, with lower-income and disadvantaged communities in the state facing disproportionate impacts.

phys-org.title: Discarded plastic bottles help save dolphins from fishing nets
phys-org.description: Newcastle University researchers have demonstrated that plastic bottles attached to fishing nets can help dolphins detect and avoid being caught and killed in the deadly gear.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Choices Shaping our Children’s Health
proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy’s Ancient Origins
proj-syn.description: The struggle between democracy and oligarchy in classical Greece was bitter, with oligarchies relying on skillfully designed political institutions to shore up unpopular regimes. As concerns grow over the “rule of the few” in the United States, Americans should consider how their own institutions are doing oligarchs’ work for them.

proj-syn.title: How Modi Has Remade India
proj-syn.description: Over the last 12 years, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has overseen dizzying progress in economic modernization and state capacity-building, as well as dismaying setbacks on institutional independence and minority inclusion. This record offers important insights into how India will navigate the 21st century.
